pageObservations.observation: Title identifies Lecture 16, Joint-Space Schemes, printed page 1.
Eight learning outcomes cover trajectory, spaces, boundary conditions, linear limitations, cubic, higher order and Python; lower-right blank rectangle has no content.
Outline lists trajectory/path/continuity, joint versus Cartesian, cubic/quintic and linear.
Defines joint trajectory theta_i(t), i=1..n, t in [0,tf], and three requirements: joint limits, bounded torque and derivative continuity.

Solid dark upper trajectory has t1,t2,t3,t4 labels between blue endpoint markers; dashed lower path has orange points but no times. These are schematic different curves, not literal same-path time scaling. Equations theta(s), theta(s(t)) are explicit.

C0,C1,C2 are position, velocity, acceleration continuity; last line incorrectly says discontinuous acceleration implies infinite torque. Finite acceleration jumps give finite torque jumps under continuous bounded model terms, not impulses.

Dynamics M(q)qdd+V(q,qd)+G(q) correctly associates acceleration discontinuity with torque discontinuity and velocity discontinuity with unbounded/impulsive acceleration. Minimum C1, preferred C2 is course guidance, not a complete sufficient bounded-acceleration proof.

Two-column table distinguishes joint coordinates versus task pose, IK and Jacobian needs, computational effort and explicit end path. No IK statement assumes joint endpoints already specified; Cartesian inverse is generally multivalued/not globally guaranteed.

Joint-position column vector and four endpoint position/velocity conditions. Blue curve overshoots final level, red dips below initial, green monotonic; same endpoints do not determine interior or smoothness.

x(t)=f(theta(t)) is explicit FK. The word unpredictable means not prescribed directly, not mathematically random. Continuous model inputs imply continuous torque only when M,V,G are continuous; friction switching omitted.
Rest-to-rest specifies initial/final positions and zero endpoint velocities, not zero accelerations. Smoothness at least C1, preferably C2.
General endpoint velocities omega0,omegaf and degree-n polynomial n+1 coefficients. Unique determination requires independent, consistent constraints, not only equal raw count.
Cubic degree3 provides four coefficients for generic four endpoint position/velocity conditions; quadratic has three. Degenerate data can reduce actual degree.
Each timed via-point interval uses a cubic. Via-point positions alone do not uniquely fix velocities, which require another assignment rule.
Derivative formulas qdot=a1+2a2t+3a3t² and qdd=2a2+6a3t; endpoint equations give a0=q0,a1=v0. Four displayed equations checked visually.

Delta theta is residual qf-q0-v0T, not raw displacement when v0 nonzero. Delta velocity=vf-v0; subtracting twice position equation from scaled velocity gives a3=Delta v/T²-2Delta theta/T³. All printed powers and signs are consistent.

Four general coefficients visibly include both endpoint velocities: a2=[3(qf-q0)-(2v0+vf)T]/T²; a3=[-2(qf-q0)+(v0+vf)T]/T³. S-shaped increasing position plot has no numeric ticks and depicts the rest-to-rest special shape, not arbitrary boundary data.
Rest-to-rest a1=0,a2=3D/T²,a3=-2D/T³ and velocity 6Dt(1-t/T)/T². Positive concave-down parabola is appropriate for D>0 only; reverse motion flips velocity sign.

Peak positive velocity occurs at T/2 with 3D/(2T); peak speed needs absolute D for reverse moves. Acceleration decreases linearly from 6D/T² to -6D/T², crosses zero at midpoint; plotted line has no ticks.

Via-point methods explicitly listed: user-specified Cartesian-to-joint mapping, heuristic assignment, acceleration-continuous spline. Local interval origin must be handled if using 0..duration coefficient formulas.

Six quintic coefficients with position, velocity, acceleration at both endpoints. Derivative factors 2,3,4,5 and 2,6,12,20 are correct; uniqueness assumes nonzero duration. Matched acceleration data can give C2 across joins, not arbitrary polynomials automatically.
Linear q=q0+(qf-q0)t/T, constant slope and zero interior acceleration. Endpoint drawing labels t0 while derivation fixes t=0; no issue if origin chosen consistently.

Endpoint hold-to-ramp velocity jump explicitly shown from 0 to D/T, then impulse discussion. Only-C0 conclusion is for the piecewise stationary extension with nonzero displacement, not the polynomial interior.
Revolute joint example:10 degrees to70 degrees over5 seconds, zero endpoint velocities; cubic chosen. These are degrees, not radians, and rest-to-rest does not impose endpoint acceleration0.
Numerical equations 25a2+125a3=60 and10a2+75a3=0; a2=-7.5a3. These come directly from final position and velocity after setting a0=10,a1=0.
Elimination gives -62.5a3=60, a3=-0.96,a2=7.2. q=10+7.2t²-.96t³, v=14.4t-2.88t², accel14.4-5.76t. Values and signs checked from actual pixels.

Actual Python code imports NumPy and pyplot; endpoints10,70,velocities0,T5. A=[[tf**2,tf**3],[2*tf,3*tf**2]], B=[theta_f-a0-a1*tf,theta_dot_f-a1], np.linalg.solve(A,B). linspace(0,tf,100) includes endpoints but excludes midpoint2.5; vectorized q,qd,qdd formulas are correct.

Actual plotting code uses figure(10,6), subplot(3,1,1/2/3), plots theta,theta_dot,theta_ddot respectively, last xlabel Time(s), tight_layout and show. No smoothing/numerical differentiation in plotting; angular-unit labels absent.

Three actual output panels: position rises10to70, velocity arch peaks approximately18 at2.5, acceleration line14.4to-14.4 crosses2.5. These plot sampled values; 100 samples cannot hit exact midpoint. Position/velocity/acceleration axis units are implicit degrees from inputs, not radian values.

Summary repeats earlier topics. Cubic acceleration continuous within one polynomial but may jump at joins/holds; quintic C2 requires matching acceleration at interfaces. Linear caveat concerns rest extension. No separate new physical concept.
Reference only: Craig2005 Introduction to Robotics,3rd edition, Pearson Prentice Hall. No new question-worthy technical content.
Thank You closing page only; no formulas or figures.

answers.reasoning: The map gives each joint coordinate at every time, not just an endpoint or torque.
Joint bounds constrain configuration, torque bounds constrain dynamics, and derivative continuity is smoothness.
An interior joint-angle violation is a kinematic violation even when endpoints are met.
Theta(s) is geometry and s(t) determines time progress along that geometry.
Continuous nondecreasing surjective time changes preserve the visited configurations and their order, not wall-clock velocities.
The four times annotate intermediate locations; the drawing does not imply stops or new joints.
Differentiate q_s sdot by product and chain rules: q_ss sdot squared plus q_s sddot.
Nested C2 requires continuity of q, qdot and qddot, not acceleration alone.
Equal positions give C0; unequal one-sided velocities prevent C1.
I alpha changes from2*1=2 to2*4=8 Nm; finite acceleration step is not a torque impulse.
A velocity step is differentiated into an acceleration impulse; an acceleration step gives a jerk impulse instead.
The printed guidance is C1 minimum and C2 preferred.
Continuous compositions and products preserve continuity only for continuous model terms and no discontinuous added effort.
Continuity controls jumps, not the numerical torque magnitude relative to an actuator bound.
Joint-space variables are joint coordinates; Cartesian variables describe tool position and orientation.
With endpoints already joint-valued, scalar interpolation avoids repeated IK along a task-space path.
The inverse notation denotes solving IK and selecting a feasible consistent branch, not guaranteed global invertibility.
A specified straight tool-tip path directly constrains task space.
Differentiating x=f(q) gives xdot=J(q)qdot for compatible velocity coordinates.
Stacking n scalar coordinates vertically gives n rows and one column.
The blue curve exceeds the dotted final-angle level before returning, demonstrating interior overshoot.
The red curve initially falls despite a higher final position, so endpoint ordering does not ensure monotonicity.
Independent coordinate parametrizations do not diagonalize the inertia matrix or remove coupled effort constraints.
Known forward kinematics maps every prescribed joint configuration to its corresponding tool pose deterministically.
A discontinuous friction contribution can add an effort jump despite smooth position derivatives.
The standard cubic endpoint data are two positions and two first derivatives.
Rest-to-rest fixes the two endpoint velocities to zero, not the entire motion.
Zero values of a function do not force its derivative to zero there; cubic endpoint acceleration is generally nonzero.
The coefficients a0 through an number n+1.
The standard minimum polynomial families have2,4,6 coefficients and corresponding independent conditions.
Equal raw counts do not exclude dependent equations or inconsistent data; full rank is required.
The stated line already satisfies all four compatible conditions; generic minimum degree need not be the actual degree.
Generic independent four endpoint conditions require four coefficients, attained by degree3.
The full cubic spans1,t,t squared,t cubed with independent coefficients.
A piecewise cubic assigns a polynomial to each interval between consecutive timed via points.
Two positions per segment leave the boundary rates undetermined unless a velocity/spline rule supplies them.
Translate absolute time by the start3s; interval length7-3=4s.
Common q and qdot ensure C1 but independent second derivatives need not agree.
Termwise differentiation gives a1+2a2t+3a3t squared.
Differentiating velocity gives2a2+6a3t.
At local t0 all positive powers vanish; q0=a0 and v0=a1.
Evaluate the cubic and its first derivative atT to obtain the displayed final-position and final-rate equations.
Each a_k t^k must have angular units, hence a2 deg/s squared and a3 deg/s cubed.
With positiveT, the residual differs from raw displacement byv0T; equality iff v0=0.
Subtract known a0 and a1 contributions from the endpoint equations, leaving the two a2,a3 equations.
Subtracting2(a2+a3T) from2a2+3a3T leaves a3T; RHS is S/T-2R/T squared.
Elimination gives a2=3D/T squared-(2v0+vf)/T.
The remaining coefficient is a3=-2D/T cubed+(v0+vf)/T squared.
Arbitrary endpoint rates can point opposite displacement; a representative S curve does not prove all cases monotone.
Rest endpoints require shape3u squared-2u cubed, with values0,1 and zero first derivatives at0,1.
Velocity6D u(1-u)/T is positive inside forD,T positive and concave down.
Atu=.5,3u squared-2u cubed=.5, so position is the average of endpoints.
D0 and both rates0 give all nonconstant coefficients0; positive duration keeps the system nonsingular.
Set qdd=6D/T squared*(1-2t/T)=0: t=T/2 andvelocity3D/(2T).
D=-60,T5 gives midpointvelocity-18; signed minimum is negative while maximum speed is18.
Evaluating the linear acceleration at0,T gives positive6D/T squared and negative6D/T squared.
Fixed normalized shape gives velocity proportional1/T and acceleration1/T squared; doublingT halves and quarters.
Differentiate acceleration6D/T squared-12Dt/T cubed once to get constantjerk-12D/T cubed.
Speed requiresT>=90/20=4.5; acceleration requiresT squared>=360/15=24; larger bound is sqrt24.
The nonzero cubic endpoint accelerations cannot match zero holds, but position and velocity do match: C1 notC2.
The source lists user-specified, heuristic and acceleration-continuous spline assignments.
Task velocity must satisfy xdot=Jqdot; select feasible joint rates before using scalar boundary velocities.
C2 adds equality of left and right second derivatives to common position and rate.
Solve-6+4v=6-4v:8v=12,v=1.5rad/s; both join accelerations become0.
A quintic supplies both endpoints with position, first derivative and second derivative data.
Differentiating a4t fourth and a5t fifth twice yields12a4t squared+20a5t cubed.
Atzero q=a0,v=a1,accel2a2; thus a2=alpha0/2.
The six constraints solve to shape10u cubed-15u fourth+6u fifth, whose first two derivatives vanish at both ends.
The holds share endpoint position and both zero derivatives, exactly the three continuity conditions.
Third derivative of normalizedshape is60-360u+360u squared; both endpoints give60D/T cubed, notzero forD nonzero.
Derivative of a linear interpolant isD/T and its second derivative vanishes in the interior.
A straight position-time segment has constant slope, which is constant joint velocity.
The hold rate0 and ramp rateD/T differ, so noC1 at that join despite continuous position.
Velocity first rises from0toD/T and later falls to0; acceleration impulses have positive and negative signed areas.
The smooth polynomial interior is distinct from its abrupt stationary extensions.
The named remedy is blending/smoothing endpoint transitions rather than instantaneous switching.
The actual example begins at10degrees,t0 and ends70degrees,t5 with both rates0.
AtT5, a2T squared+a3T cubed=60 and2a2T+3a3T squared=0, yielding25/125 and10/75.
Eliminate a2=-7.5a3; -62.5a3=60 gives-.96 andthen7.2.
The example has6*60/25=14.4 atstart and its negative atend.
Evaluate10+7.2-.96=16.24degrees; polynomial arithmetic preserves consistently chosen angle units without trigonometric conversion.
The code uses NumPy array creation/linear algebra and pyplot figure/axes commands.
SubstitutingT5 givesA[[25,125],[10,75]], residualB[70-10,0]=[60,0].
The solve finds a vectorx satisfyingAx=B, then unpacks its two entries intoa2,a3.
The2x2 determinant is3T fourth-2T fourth=T fourth, nonzero forT>0.
T0 makesA allzero whileB remains[60,0]; NumPy solve raises singular matrix error rather than inventing an infinite solution.
The a1T term is the known displacement contribution from the initial rate and must be removed from the residual.
linspace with defaultendpointtrue gives100 inclusive samples across99 gaps, spacing5/99.
NumPy power on the1D timearray acts elementwise; no matrix powers or differentiation occur.
The1D100element timearray remains shape(100,) under scalar coefficient broadcast and elementwise arithmetic.
The program evaluates analytically differentiated polynomials, not finite differences or plotted pixels.
Samples are5k/99;k49and50 give245/99and250/99, and nointegerk gives2.5.
Velocity=18-2.88(t-2.5) squared. Nearest offset5/198 yields loss18/99 squared, giving17.9981634527.
subplot arguments specify3rows1column and second1-indexed axes.
The three successive plot calls displaytheta,theta_dot,theta_ddot top tobottom.
Matplotlib figsize dimensions are physical inches,10wide6high; pixel dimensions additionally dependonDPI.
Raw strings preserve backslashes for mathtext rather than triggering Python escapes; no unit conversion.
tight_layout adjusts axes spacing; show requests figure display.
The code creates a single figure with threeaxes and contains no print or savefig call.
The plotted position increases10to70,velocitypositivearch,andaccelerationlinear decreasingthroughzero agreewith the source example.
Velocity derivative equals acceleration, so itszero crossing positive-to-negative identifies interiorvelocitymaximum.
The input angles10and70are degrees, and time is seconds; derivative units followdegrees/sanddegrees/s squared.
Each polynomial has continuous acceleration internally; separate polynomial pieces require matching one-sided accelerations forC2.
Firstsegmentendaccel=-6,secondstartaccel=+6;sharedposition1andrates0 giveC1notC2.
Degreefive permits acceleration matching butdoesnotimpose it automatically; all three shared endpointdata must agree.
